root_idea.summary: Rain descending from the sky, reaching and benefiting the land.
root_idea.development: The central rain sense extends to watering land and people, rain characterized by aid or productivity, and consequent growth such as herbage. Other attested derivatives develop specialized or figurative meanings.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Distinct Quran-attested passive verbal construction, presented under the normalized Form IV perfect citation form.

senses.definition: To provide with rain; in the passive, to be given rain.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence is the passive imperfect يُغَاثُ and describes people receiving rain. The supplied lexical evidence attests the corresponding construction of sending rain upon or raining upon people.

senses.definition: Rain; rain descending from the sky.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic uses denote rain generally. A more specialized classical qualification of rain as especially beneficial or aid-bringing is listed separately under broader Classical Arabic meanings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To water land with rain or send rain upon people; said also of rain falling upon land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I verb. Passive constructions describe land or people being rained upon.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek, search, or grope for a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II usage explicitly applied to a blind man.
A Form V usage said of a camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rain characterized as productive of much good or as bringing aid and succour.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A classical qualification of the rain term, also attested in the phrase غَيْثٌ مُغِيثٌ; the aid-bearing qualification is associated with the notion of succour.
An idiomatic tropical designation, linked to the bee's pursuit of vegetation and flowers that follow rain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Herbage growing by means of rainwater.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Tropical usage in which the product is named for its cause.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Water beneath a stratum of rock; hence, a well having a constant accession of water.
Of a horse, one that performs or increases its running from run to run.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Tropical usage describing sustained or increasing performance.
Participial or adjectival description of rain-watered land.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Rain-watering and passive rain-upon constructions are represented.
Specialized Form II seeking or groping meaning represented.
Form V becoming fat meaning represented.
Inflectional statement identifying a verbal noun; it adds no independent lexical meaning.
Rain sense and beneficial or aid-bringing qualification represented.
Aid-bringing or beneficial rain phrase represented.
Pointer-only cross-reference to the preceding rain-watered-land expression.

cautions: The specialized aid-bringing qualification in غَيْثٌ مُغِيثٌ is presented separately because the supplied discussion relates the epithet مُغِيثٌ to the غوث notion of aid.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The Quranic surface form يُغَاثُ is homographic with the passive rain-upon construction recorded under Form I غَاثَ, while the supplied QAC analysis classifies the Quranic group as Form IV. The rain-provision meaning is assigned, but the correspondence between the two derivational analyses is not independently resolved by the packet.
